decisive_wording: C: "shows a vision-language model AnyGrasp's candidate grasps ... then tuned prompts so the model picks the right grasp more often" vs A: "so it picks correctly more often" and B: "tuned its prompts so it chooses correctly"
info_preserved_or_lost: All three keep PhD-led/ICLR context, AnyGrasp, Open3D overlays, multi-camera images, VLM selection and prompt tuning. A and B leave the object of 'picks/chooses correctly' implicit; C states it is the right grasp. B's 'renders' is a slightly stronger mechanism verb than C's 'shows'.
credibility_change: Roughly equal; C's 'the model picks the right grasp' gives a clearer, defensible success criterion for an interview discussion.
readability_change: C resolves the ambiguous pronouns in A ('it' could be the pipeline) and B ('its prompts'/'it chooses'), so a recruiter can restate it on one read.

decisive_wording: C: "rates research documents by importance: on an EventBridge schedule a larger LLM grades its ratings" vs A's missing EventBridge and B's "document-importance classifier" / "grades the classifier"
info_preserved_or_lost: A drops EventBridge (a keyword and the scheduling mechanism). B keeps EventBridge but compresses the purpose into the noun stack 'document-importance classifier' and drops 'research'. C keeps Bedrock, research-document importance rating, EventBridge, LLM-as-grader and threshold-gated fine-tuning.
credibility_change: C and B name the real scheduling mechanism; C also says what is graded (its ratings), which is more precise than B's 'grades the classifier'. A is less concrete about how scheduling works.
readability_change: C reads as one plain sentence with a colon; A's interrupting 'hosted on Amazon Bedrock' clause and 'scheduled grades of its output' are harder to parse; B's split into two sentences and noun stack add effort.

decisive_wording: A: "Cut the time for AI to generate a workflow 65%" vs B: "Cut AI workflow generation time 65%"
info_preserved_or_lost: Both keep the 65% / under 15s metric, Claude skill, sub-skills, Python tools, CloudWatch and OpenSearch. B adds 'workflow' before 'search and validation', a small specificity gain.
